text: Should you use your browser's VPN? Firefox added a VPN to their browser earlier this year and I haven't really talked about it. So let's chat about browser VPNs, shall we? So there's regular VPNs and there's browser VPNs. A regular VPN app routes and encrypts all network traffic from your phone or computer, including background apps or any other app that you might have opened like an email client or even a game. A browser VPN only works inside your browser. Other apps or other browsers on your device are not being protected while you're using a specific browser's built in VPN. Most people who are big on cybersecurity will recommend that you use a full-blown VPN app rather than a browser's built in VPN. Granted, some security is better than no security. So if our options are no VPN or browser VPN, browser VPN wins. But a dedicated VPN app will almost always be better. They use robust encryption protocols, whereas built in browser VPNs are essentially just proxies rather than VPNs. It'll mask your IP address, but it is more vulnerable to DNS and data leaks compared to a true VPN. Once again, from the top, a true VPN is more secure, but a browser VPN is better than nothing. Or really, it's just better for like certain tasks. So do you use a regular VPN, a browser VPN, or are you just raw-dogging the internet? Let me know in the comments.
